items.stem: ‘The revolutions of 1848-49 in Italy and Germany failed mainly because of divisions among the revolutionaries.’ How far do you agree with this view?
items.answer: For: Liberals and radicals disagreed over aims and methods. Germans divided over Grossdeutschland and Kleindeutschland. Italians divided between monarchists and republicans and between states. Against: The armies of Austria and Prussia remained loyal to their rulers. Foreign intervention, especially France in Rome, crushed revolutions. The rulers recovered once the shock of March 1848 passed. Judgement: divisions weakened the revolutions, but they failed because the old regimes kept control of military force.

items.stem: ‘Cavour was the main architect of Italian unification.’ How far do you agree?
items.answer: For: He modernised Piedmont and made it the leader of Italian liberalism. He won French support at Plombières and so defeated Austria in 1859. He annexed the central duchies and the Papal States to control the process. Against: Garibaldi conquered the south, which Cavour had not planned to take. Foreign powers, especially France and Prussia, made unification possible. Mazzini's ideas had spread the idea of a united Italy. Judgement: Cavour shaped the form unification took under Piedmont, but he was not its only architect: the south was won by Garibaldi and Venetia and Rome by events abroad.

items.stem: ‘Bismarck planned German unification from the start.’ Discuss.
items.answer: For: His "iron and blood" speech showed he expected unification by force. Each war prepared the way for the next. He manipulated the Ems Telegram to provoke war with France. Against: His first aim was Prussian dominance in north Germany, not national unity. He responded to opportunities such as the Schleswig-Holstein crisis and the Spanish succession. Economic and military developments outside his control mattered. Judgement: Bismarck aimed consistently at Prussian power, but he was an opportunist who exploited events rather than following a plan for unification.

items.answer: For: The Zollverein tied the German states to Prussia economically. Industrial growth, coal and railways supported a modern army. Prussian wealth paid for army reform. Judgement: economic strength gave Prussia the means, but unification was achieved through Bismarck's diplomacy and military victory.

items.stem: What is meant by “Risorgimento”?
options: The peace of 1866 that ended the Austro-Prussian War and excluded Austria from German affairs.
The report of July 1870 that Bismarck edited to make it seem that the king had insulted the French ambassador.
The German National Association founded in 1859 to promote unity under Prussia.
The "resurgence", the nineteenth-century movement for Italian unification and national revival.
items.answer: The "resurgence", the nineteenth-century movement for Italian unification and national revival.
items.markingKey: Risorgimento: the "resurgence", the nineteenth-century movement for Italian unification and national revival. [1]

items.stem: Which of these events happened first?
options: The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed
The Battles of Magenta and Solferino were fought
items.answer: Piedmont joined the Crimean War
items.markingKey: Piedmont joined the Crimean War (1855); the Battles of Magenta and Solferino were fought (1859); the Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed (March 1861); Italian troops entered Rome (September 1870). [1]

items.stem: A revision guide lists these reasons why Garibaldi's expedition of 1860 succeeded. A: The Neapolitan army was poorly led and demoralised. B: Cavour allowed the expedition to sail. C: Sicilian peasants had risen against Bourbon rule. Explain how these reasons were linked and decide which mattered most.
items.answer: Any reasoned choice. A: The Neapolitan army was poorly led and demoralised. B: Cavour allowed the expedition to sail. C: Sicilian peasants had risen against Bourbon rule. Possible judgement: Garibaldi's leadership was crucial, but the weakness of the Bourbon state made his success possible.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a choice; up to 3 marks for explaining it with precise detail; up to 2 marks for comparing it with the other reasons [6]

items.stem: To what extent was Italian unification achieved by foreign powers rather than by Italians?
items.answer: For: French armies defeated Austria in 1859. Prussia's victory gave Italy Venetia in 1866. French withdrawal in 1870 allowed the capture of Rome. Against: Cavour's diplomacy secured French help. Garibaldi and the Thousand conquered the south. Plebiscites showed support in central and southern Italy. Judgement: Italians provided the leadership and won the south, but at each stage of the war against Austria and for Rome foreign powers were decisive.

Level 2 (6-9): mainly descriptive, with implicit links to the question. Level 1 (1-5): general assertions with little accurate knowledge. Agree / supporting: French armies defeated Austria in 1859. Prussia's victory gave Italy Venetia in 1866. French withdrawal in 1870 allowed the capture of Rome. Disagree / other factors: Cavour's diplomacy secured French help. Garibaldi and the Thousand conquered the south. Plebiscites showed support in central and southern Italy. Possible judgement: Italians provided the leadership and won the south, but at each stage of the war against Austria and for Rome foreign powers were decisive. [20]

items.stem: Study Sources B and D. It is the duty of every Italian to help them with words, money and arms.” To what extent do Sources B and D agree about Italian unification?
items.answer: Source B: It suggests Cavour admired Garibaldi but feared his march on Rome would provoke France. Source D: It shows Garibaldi presenting the Sicilian revolt as a national Italian cause. Differences in authorship, date and purpose explain the contrast.

items.stem: A revision guide lists these reasons why the southern German states joined the German Empire in 1871. A: France was seen as the aggressor after the Ems Telegram. B: Bismarck offered concessions such as Bavaria keeping some rights. C: The Zollverein had tied their economies to the north. Which was the most significant? Explain your answer with reference to the other reasons.
items.answer: Any reasoned choice. A: France was seen as the aggressor after the Ems Telegram. B: Bismarck offered concessions such as Bavaria keeping some rights. C: The Zollverein had tied their economies to the north. Possible judgement: war with France created the national feeling and the circumstances that made it impossible for the south to stay out.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a choice; up to 3 marks for explaining it with precise detail; up to 2 marks for comparing it with the other reasons [6]

items.stem: Study Sources C and D. Source C: Bismarck, Reflections and Reminiscences, published 1898 (summary). In his memoirs Bismarck presented the wars of 1864, 1866 and 1870 as steps in a deliberate policy that he had pursued from the start to unite Germany under Prussia. Source D: Bismarck, speech to the budget committee of the Prussian Landtag, September 1862 (translated, abridged). “The great questions of the day will not be decided by speeches and majority decisions - that was the great mistake of 1848 and 1849 - but by iron and blood.” Identify one similarity and one difference between Sources C and D on German unification.
items.answer: Source C: It presents unification as the result of a long-term plan by Bismarck. Source D: Bismarck argues that power and force, not parliamentary debate, will decide Germany's future. A similarity and a difference must each be supported by details from both sources.

items.stem: Historians have offered several reasons why Prussian liberals came to support Bismarck after 1866. A: The North German Confederation had a parliament elected by universal male suffrage. B: Bismarck offered the Indemnity Bill as a reconciliation. C: Many liberals valued unity above constitutional principles. Explain how these reasons were linked and decide which mattered most.
items.answer: Any reasoned choice. A: The North German Confederation had a parliament elected by universal male suffrage. B: Bismarck offered the Indemnity Bill as a reconciliation. C: Many liberals valued unity above constitutional principles. Possible judgement: success in 1866 persuaded many liberals that national unity mattered more than parliamentary control.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a choice; up to 3 marks for explaining it with precise detail; up to 2 marks for comparing it with the other reasons [6]

items.stem: Explain why the revolutions in Italy failed by 1849.
items.answer: Austrian military strength under Radetzky defeated Piedmont at Custoza and Novara. Italian states and leaders were divided in aims, between monarchists and republicans. The pope withdrew support in April 1848. France intervened to crush the Roman Republic. The peasantry gave little support. Judgement: Austrian military power was decisive, but divisions among Italians meant they could not resist it.

items.stem: Kwame is planning an answer to the question: “How far did the 1848 revolutions change the prospects for unification in Italy and Germany?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Kwame could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: 1848 failed in the short term, but it pointed both movements towards leadership by Piedmont and Prussia. Support: Piedmont kept the Statuto and became the leader of Italian liberals. The failure of idealism discredited Mazzini's methods and encouraged realism. Challenge: Austria restored its dominance in both Italy and Germany by 1850. Olmütz showed Prussia could not yet challenge Austria.
items.markingKey: 2 marks for a line of argument that answers the question directly and is sustainable; 1 mark for each relevant supporting point and 1 for each challenging point [6]

items.stem: What is meant by “Plombières agreement”?
options: The all-German national assembly elected in 1848 to draw up a constitution for a united Germany.
The union of German states north of the River Main under Prussian leadership, set up in 1867.
The secret deal of 1858 in which Napoleon III promised to help Piedmont fight Austria in return for Nice and Savoy.
The law of 1866 by which the Prussian liberals approved Bismarck's unconstitutional spending, splitting the liberals.
items.answer: The secret deal of 1858 in which Napoleon III promised to help Piedmont fight Austria in return for Nice and Savoy.
items.markingKey: Plombières agreement: the secret deal of 1858 in which Napoleon III promised to help Piedmont fight Austria in return for Nice and Savoy. [1]

items.stem: Ravi is planning an answer to the question: “‘Unification in both Italy and Germany was driven more by Realpolitik than by nationalism.’ How far do you agree?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Ravi could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: Realpolitik delivered unification, but leaders could exploit nationalism because it had become a powerful idea among the educated classes. Support: Cavour and Bismarck used diplomacy and war to expand Piedmont and Prussia. Foreign alliances and wars were decisive. Challenge: Garibaldi's campaign and plebiscites showed nationalist support. Nationalist feeling made the southern German states join in 1870.
items.markingKey: 2 marks for a line of argument that answers the question directly and is sustainable; 1 mark for each relevant supporting point and 1 for each challenging point [6]

items.stem: Priya is planning an answer to the question: “To what extent were the outcomes of unification in Italy and Germany similar?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Priya could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: the processes were similar in reliance on a leading state and war, but the resulting states differed greatly in strength and structure. Support: Both were achieved under a dominant northern state and monarchy. Both depended on war and foreign diplomacy. Challenge: Germany was a federation; Italy a centralised state. Germany was achieved by Prussian military power; Italy owed more to foreign help and Garibaldi.
